subtitle: Lesson 20 · Regulatory Compliance Frameworks

code:
Control: quarterly access review
  (manager confirms each person's access still fits their role)

maps to:
  SOC 2          -> Security criterion, logical access evidence
  ISO 27001      -> Annex A access-rights review control
  PCI DSS        -> need-to-know access, reviewed periodically (if in CDE)
caption: One review, one piece of evidence, reused across three separate audits.

steps.label: One real control, implemented once
steps.sub: not four separate access-review processes for four audits

steps.label: The crosswalk makes it explicit
steps.sub: one row per control, columns for each framework's matching requirement

steps.label: Adding a framework gets cheaper over time
steps.sub: most of the engineering work is already done after the first one

code:
gap types to watch for:
  - evidence depth    (PCI may need encryption-algorithm detail; access review alone may not)
  - scope mismatch     ("production systems" broadly vs. the narrower CDE)
  - cadence mismatch   (build to the STRICTEST required cadence, never the loosest)
caption: A real crosswalk documents these gaps honestly instead of papering over them.
